description: rebaseWhen=conflicted, not the default 'auto'. With automerge on, 'auto' means
'behind-base-branch': every merge to main leaves the other open PRs behind, so
Renovate force-pushes all of them, re-runs their checks, and blocks automerge
until each goes green again. Draining a queue of N PRs then costs ~N^2/2
force-pushes and notifications, and merges one PR per Renovate run. These stacks
touch disjoint files and never actually conflict, so rebasing buys nothing.

packageRules.description: Postgres major upgrades require a manual pg_dump/restore migration — recreating on a new major breaks the data dir. Don't propose them.
MariaDB major upgrades need a mariadb-upgrade pass over the on-disk data dir — recreating on a new major is not enough. Don't propose them.
Require manual review for pocket-id (auth provider — outage locks out all services)
Require manual review for immich (postgres DB migrations can be irreversible)
Require manual review for traefik majors (gateway — outage takes down everything)
Group gluetun and qBittorrent — qBittorrent runs inside gluetun's network namespace, so the pair is recreated together anyway.

linuxserver/qbittorrent also publishes old Ubuntu-release tags (20.04.1, ...) that sort as 'major 20' — #224 'upgraded' 5.2.4 to a 2021 build of qBittorrent 4.3.9. Only allow real qBittorrent versions.

Require manual review for frigate. Every minor rewrites the config schema (0.17 replaced record.retain, 0.18 reworked genai/masks) and the config models are extra=forbid, so a bad bump means the stack won't start. 0.x tags make those minors, not majors, so the global major rule never catches them. config/config.yml.tpl's `version:` must be hand-migrated in the same PR.
Group the grimmory app and its MariaDB into one PR — a bump that moves only one of the pair still has to boot against the other.

Require manual review for mcp-servers. Each container holds live credentials to a homelab control plane (Home Assistant, UniFi, Proxmox, AdGuard), several of these projects are small single-maintainer repos, and the tool surface a bump exposes goes straight to the internet-facing MCP portal — bumps get eyes on them.
Never open digest-only PRs — upstream image rebuilds create constant churn with no version change. All images are pinned to real tags.
